answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am write this letter for complain about your buses in the evening, because two month it is very bad situation for me and for other passenger.

Firstly, I take the number 46 bus from the city centre to Ashford Road. I finish my work in six o'clock and I take always this bus, five days in a week. It is the only one bus for my area, so I have not another choice.

Secondly, the bus come very late or sometime it don't come at all. Last week I waiting almost fifty minutes in the bus stop and the weather was very cold. I arrive to my home in half past eight and my family eat the dinner without me. It's been awful for us. One day I must to take a taxi and I pay eighteen pounds, this is too much money for one journey. Also I am tired in the next morning because I sleep late.

Thirdly, please do something for this problem, we are waiting your answer.

Best wishes,

Kerem Aydin

why_this_band.task_response: The first two points are addressed in detail (route, time, frequency, wait, taxi fare), but the third point is squeezed into a single sentence: please do something for this problem is not a request the company could act on. A formal complaint letter closes with It's been awful and Best wishes, so the register does not stay consistent throughout.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly pattern marks only sequence, not the logic of the paragraphs, and the third settles into a one-sentence paragraph. The information is still trackable, though, so the reader does not lose the letter's purpose.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Vocabulary meets the task's most basic needs, but bus, very, problem repeat, and there is no formal letter phrasing at all. Choices such as very bad situation, too much money for one journey give the reader roughly the right meaning, not precision.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Almost every sentence has an error: I am write, for complain, in six o'clock, it don't come, I waiting, I must to take, two month. Structures are largely simple sentences and sequences joined with so; there is next to no subordination.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Turn the third point into a concrete request: state what is being asked for (written explanation, correction of the timetable, an extra service) and when it is expected. Closing with Yours faithfully would also fix the register.

answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the evening service on the number 46 route, which I use to travel home from my work five days in a week.

I take the 46 from the city centre to Ashford Road at about six o'clock every weekday evening. I have used this bus for three years and until this summer it was reliable. However, for the last two months it has arrived fifteen or twenty minutes late almost every evening, and on several occasion it did not come at all. Nobody at the bus stop knows the reason and there is no information on the sign.

This situation has caused me a number of problem. Last Tuesday I waited fifty minutes in very cold weather, and twice I had to take a taxi, which cost me nearly twenty pounds each time. I have also arrived late to my evening class at the community college two times, and the teacher has warned me about my attendance.

I would be grateful if you can explain what has changed on this route and when the normal timetable will come back. If the service cannot be improved quickly, I would like the company to consider to add an extra bus at half past six.

Yours faithfully,

Kerem Aydin

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are addressed and the request is concrete (explanation, restoring the timetable, an extra service), and the register stays formal throughout. The description of the journey is a little thin: frequency is given, but there is no detail that would strengthen the letter, such as why this service is the only option.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The paragraphing maps onto the points exactly and is easy to read, but the transitions follow the However / This situation / I would be grateful pattern, and every paragraph opens the same way. Linking words are used correctly, with limited variety.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items suited to the task's register are present — reliable, attendance, timetable, I would be grateful if. In places such as consider to add and will come back, the collocation and form do not quite settle.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The present perfect, a relative clause and a conditional clause are used under control; most sentences are error-free. The remaining errors (five days in a week, on several occasion, a number of problem, consider to add) never block meaning.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Tie the complaint to a consequence: bring together how much the delay has cost and what was missed in one place, and add a date to the request. Clearing up the plural and verb-pattern errors (occasion, problem, consider adding) would move the grammar up one band.

answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about the evening service on the number 46 route between the city centre and Ashford Road, which has become badly unreliable over the past two months.

I catch the 46 shortly after six o'clock on every weekday, as it is the only direct service to my part of the town and there is no rail alternative. Until the beginning of June it kept to the timetable closely enough for me to plan the rest of my evening around it. Since then it has rarely arrived within twenty minutes of the advertised time, and on at least six occasions it has not appeared at all, with no announcement at the stop and nothing on your website.

The consequences have gone well beyond mild inconvenience. I have twice been forced to take a taxi at a cost of nearly twenty pounds, I have missed two sessions of an evening course that I pay for by the term, and waiting for the best part of an hour at an unsheltered stop in cold weather is not something I can go on doing through the winter.

I would therefore be grateful for a written explanation of what has changed on this route, together with a firm date by which the published timetable will be restored. If the demand in the early evening now exceeds the capacity you have allocated to it, I would ask you to consider a second departure at around half past six.

Yours faithfully,

Kerem Aydin

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are developed and each carries information the reader can act on: the route and frequency, an outcome measured in money and missed classes, a two-part request asking for a written reply and a date. The register stays formal and measured throughout; the complaint stays forceful without turning harsh.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The letter follows the logic of the complaint: first the journey, then when the deterioration began, then the cost, and the request at the very end. Connectors such as therefore and since then do the sentence's work rather than decorating the start of a paragraph.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items such as advertised time, unsheltered stop, by the term, exceeds the capacity appear with the right collocation and suit the formal register. Badly unreliable feels a little strained; the rest of the choices are natural.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses, a conditional clause and a noun clause are controlled; long sentences proceed without losing structure. Errors are rare and do not stop the reader, but the flexibility does not reach the naturalness of band 9.

answers.what_would_lift_it: At this level the gain is in compression, not extra detail: bring the three outcomes in the third paragraph into a shorter sentence and give the request a measurable timeframe (for example, ten working days).
